about: Every OBP-API call the tokenizer makes, all through internal/obp/client.go: verb, path (OBP placeholders in capitals; ENTITY is one of the entity names in internal/obp/client.go), the source file and the text that makes the call (needles), and the response fields the code reads. scripts/create_test_data.py, which seeds test data, is not listed. internal/obp/contract_test.go checks this list against the source and against snapshot.json, which obp-api-contract/snapshot.py writes from an OBP-API's resource docs. The reads are kept by hand: the DirectLogin answer is decoded into an unnamed struct and the dynamic entity answers are unwrapped from a map by entity name, so no named struct maps one-to-one to an entry and the reads are not compared with json tags.
version_policy: Each call writes the OBP-API version it needs in its own path. One configured version cannot serve them all, because an endpoint exists only in the versions OBP-API documents it for. The contract test checks every call against the endpoint documented for the version it names and fails on any version below v5.1.0. To move a call to a newer version, change its path and run snapshot.py again.

calls.note: Declares the Scopes the tokenizer needs. OBP-API refuses it until an administrator has marked the app's Consumer as a Platform App, and the answer says which Scopes the app holds.
Filtered by status_code, parcel_id or activity_id. Each record is decoded into its type in internal/obp/types.go.
calls.undocumented_endpoint: dynamic entity, defined at run time

calls.note: The record under the entity name is decoded into its type in internal/obp/types.go, and the raw body is hashed (keccak256) into the token's integrity hash. The same URL is stored on-chain as the record's link.
